instrumentDefect.defect: k6_price claim 2, one_turn_affords_one_verb, counted a control RETURNING TRUE as a verb having been bought. 9C deliberately made two picker openers free, so after the one paid court verb, open_heir_picker and open_scheme_picker still succeeded and k6 scored 4/5. instrumentDefect.fix: k6 now counts a second purchase only when attention fell or a seat changed - judged by simulation delta, the same discipline g2/g5/g6 already use - and prints the free navigation separately by name. instrumentDefect.lesson: A gate that measures PRICE must count what was bought, not what returned True. Every time this arc has made a control free, a gate that conflated 'succeeded' with 'spent' has gone red for the wrong reason.

instrumentDefect: d3_alone built its pytest nodeid as '<file>::<funcname>' from an ast.walk, dropping the enclosing class. CynCo organised the new cases into TestEmptyTableLayout / TestPowersTableEmpty / TestEndingOverlay, so every nodeid was NOT FOUND, pytest exited non-zero having run nothing, and the gate reported all 20 green cases as red-when-alone. Verified before believing it: the file runs 20 passed in 1.48s, and the class-qualified nodeid passes alone. Fixed between runs by walking ClassDef ancestry into the nodeid; the rule is unchanged and is now enforceable on class-nested tests it previously could not address. Third instrument defect of this project, after g6's rolling calibration anchor and k6 counting a True return as a purchase - all three shared the shape of a gate whose blindness masqueraded as the agent's failure.
finding: Two defects, both present since long before this wave, both invisible to every gate written through Stage 9 because all of them draw the page at TURN 1 and stop. (1) broadsheet.py:2028 guarded the COLUMN index and never the ROW index when reading text_rects[0][i]; Table.layout returns text_rects == [] for a table with no data rows, so a House owning zero enterprises made the defensive expression itself raise IndexError - 23 crashes on the Enterprises tab from turn 49 of 70 with game_over still None. (2) endings.py judge() was finished, correct, and imported by console.py and by nothing in gilded/ui/ - seventy turns of play paid out as one Gazette line, 'THE AGE CLOSES: century', among 210 strings. Now a full closing page drawn from game_over alone, epilogue judged once and cached, carrying the ending name, the engine's own four paragraphs and all four axis scores. endings.py, chassis.py and docket.py untouched.

handGrade.note: The recorded verified:false is CORRECT as an outcome — the wave never committed — but it is NOT a measure of the work. Graded by hand against the working tree the wave left behind, g9 stands 6/8, up from 1/8. Four of the five claims it was sent to fix are green: every petition now carries a real Character, every such person is named where the player reads, every one reaches the drawn page, and the marriage offer names both sides. Share of the dominant kind fell 29% -> 24%.
handGrade.rootCause: F73. g9 measured both sides with `git archive`, so it could only see COMMITTED trees. The wave's work was uncommitted for the whole run, REV therefore resolved to the same sha as BASE, and the gate's self-scoring guard fired on every consultation: 'Refusing to score the base against itself', SystemExit(2). The wave could not tell 'my work is red' from 'this instrument will not answer' and spent 500 turns — the driver's cap, not a crash — blind on its primary objective. Instrument fixed: REV is now the working tree; BASE is still pinned and still exported from git.
instrumentDefectsFound: g9 claim 1 counted seat_vacancy's {'candidates': [Character, ...]} as faceless because it never looked inside a list — contradicting trap T2 of the brief it was grading. Fixed: actor sequences are descended into.

g9's 'is this person named?' test read p.text alone, when seat_vacancy names its candidates in the OPTION LABELS the player chooses between. Fixed: the readable surface is the prompt plus its options.
genuineRedsRemaining: REGRESSION, must not ship: the page says 'Cleopatra Ashworth marries Ramses Vantrell' and the engine says 'Ramses Ashworth weds Astrid Vantrell'. _accept still calls arrange_match_between (which re-picks by bloodline_quality), so the wed_match seam the wave wrote is dead code; and wed_match itself carries a silent fallback that weds a different couple when the named pair is unavailable. Naming the wrong couple is worse than naming nobody.
Variety untouched: still 7 distinct kinds across a century, needs 9.

handGrade.note: Zero commits, zero movement. The wave wrote FIVE new petition generators (_gen_stress_crisis, _gen_courtier_grievance, _gen_province_unrest, _gen_diplomatic_overturn, _gen_dividend_review), never registered a single one of them in generate_petitions, and then reverted them out of docket.py before the 500-turn cap. Verified at run end: the file holds only the original nine _gen_* functions. The only surviving change is an uncommitted re-baseline of test_treasury_journal.py plus three scratch probe scripts in the repo root. The six claims green at HEAD are still green because HEAD never moved.
handGrade.rootCause: F74 recurrence, third consecutive. Two compounding failures: (1) the generators were DEAD CODE the entire time they existed — writing a _gen_* function is not adding a petition kind, registering it in generate_petitions' tuple is, and no run of this stage has ever done that; (2) the wave then self-reverted its own new code, exactly as 11B did via docket_base.py, despite the 11C brief banning scratch snapshots of docket.py by name. Naming the trap in the brief was not sufficient on its own — same lesson as brief-authoring rule 7.
